_about: Transcription of the Mantis review packet at competitor/out/report.md. Same findings, same order, same ratings - not a second analysis.
_toolkit: Mantis skills (google/mantis), stages run: architecture, threat-model, plan, researcher, dedupe, review, critic, calibrate, report.
_severity_scale: Mantis priority buckets from mantis-calibrate step 4: CRITICAL 8.0-10.0, HIGH 6.0-7.9, MEDIUM 3.0-5.9, LOW 0.1-2.9. Score = (Impact + Likelihood) * Context Multiplier, then the 27 sanity caps.
_deviations: mantis-reproduce and mantis-patch were NOT run - outside the engagement authorization (file subset, no build, no runtime). No finding carries empirical execution evidence.

Because of that, no finding can exceed the mantis-calibrate Category B rule 1 static cap (likelihood <= 3, x0.8 hazard, CRITICAL forbidden). Nothing reached HIGH; that is a ceiling of the method under these constraints, not a statement that nothing serious is present.
The three findings marked repro_status=not_attempted were force-downgraded to LOW 2.0 by Category A rule 1. Their uncapped hazard is given so the downgrade is auditable.

mantis-report step 1.4 would have excluded every finding here (it admits only reproduced findings, or statically_confirmed ones carrying a stack/sanitizer trace). Deviating from that predicate was necessary for the packet to exist at all; noted in the report.
_target_root: extern3/new-api/target (paths below are relative to it)

findings.title: Handler controller.GetUserGroups is registered a second time at /api/user/groups with no authentication middleware
findings.impact: An unauthenticated internet caller reaches an endpoint the codebase elsewhere guards with UserAuth. Depending on the absent handler this yields either disclosure of the group/pricing-tier configuration to anonymous users, or handler execution against a zero/absent user identity.
findings.evidence: Line 77 `userRoute.GET("/groups", controller.GetUserGroups)` has no auth middleware in its chain - `userRoute` (line 66) never calls `Use()`. Line 82 `selfRoute.GET("/self/groups", controller.GetUserGroups)` binds the SAME handler symbol inside `selfRoute`, whose `Use(middleware.UserAuth())` is at line 80, before the registration, so it applies. One handler, two registrations, one of them unauthenticated.

findings.title: SESSION_SECRET placeholder guard is unreachable when the variable is unset, and CryptoSecret silently reuses the same key
findings.impact: An operator who never sets SESSION_SECRET boots with a build-time constant secret and receives zero warning. An external attacker who knows that constant can forge session cookies for any user id, including the root account, with no credentials and no user interaction -- a total authentication bypass of every UserAuth/AdminAuth/RootAuth route in router/api-router.go. Because CryptoSecret defaults to the same value, the same knowledge also breaks whatever the application encrypts (channel keys, tokens, OAuth state), and rotating one secret cannot be done without rotating the other.
findings.evidence: The `if ss == "random_string"` rejection (line 51) and its `log.Fatal` (line 54) sit inside `if os.Getenv("SESSION_SECRET") != "" {` opened at line 49, with no else clause; line 62 then reads `CryptoSecret = SessionSecret`.

findings.title: User API token key retrieval omits the SecureVerificationRequired step-up that the identically shaped channel key route enforces
findings.impact: A3 (attacker holding a stolen or hijacked session) converts a transient, revocable foothold into permanent credentials. API token keys are long-lived bearer credentials for paid inference: unlike the session, they survive logout, password reset and re-authentication, so the victim's normal remediation does not evict the attacker. Line 281 drains every key the account holds in a single request, so the window needed is one HTTP round trip. The financial exposure is direct (paid inference billed to the victim) and the KB threat model classifies these two routes' asset as CRITICAL, noting that the step-up already applied to the channel key 'sets the bar for the rest'.
findings.evidence: `middleware.SecureVerificationRequired()` occurs exactly once in the file, at line 235 on `channelRoute.POST("/:id/key", ...)`. Lines 276 and 281 (`tokenRoute.POST("/:id/key", ...)` and `tokenRoute.POST("/batch/keys", ...)`) carry the same `CriticalRateLimit()` + `DisableCache()` pair but omit the step-up; line 64 shows the step-up is wired at the user tier.

findings.title: Bulk channel-key management is admin-only while reading a single channel key requires root plus step-up verification
findings.impact: A merely-admin account (below the root tier the authors reserved for single-key access) reaches the bulk key-management surface without step-up verification, undermining the protection deliberately placed on the single-key route.
findings.evidence: Both routes are in the `AdminAuth()` group opened at line 228. Line 235 adds RootAuth + CriticalRateLimit + DisableCache + SecureVerificationRequired; line 264 `channelRoute.POST("/multi_key/manage", controller.ManageMultiKeys)` adds nothing.
findings.sanity_triage_applied: High-Privilege External Access; Equivalent Primitives; Static Confirmation

findings.title: Unauthenticated /api/ratio_config exposes pricing data that the sibling /api/pricing route gates behind HeaderNavModuleAuth
findings.impact: Anonymous disclosure of model ratio/pricing configuration, bypassing the operator's own visibility control for the pricing module. Competitive/commercial exposure rather than direct compromise.
findings.evidence: Line 33 gates /pricing with `middleware.HeaderNavModuleAuth("pricing")` and line 35 gates /perf-metrics with the PublicOrUserAuth variant of the same module key, but line 54 `apiRouter.GET("/ratio_config", middleware.CriticalRateLimit(), controller.GetRatioConfig)` has no module check and no auth.

findings.title: Unauthenticated POST /api/setup carries none of the abuse controls the codebase applies to public account creation
findings.impact: Exposes the privilege-bootstrap path to A1, the unauthenticated network attacker the KB ranks highest for this subset, with no rate limit to slow repeated attempts and no captcha to stop automation. Because `GlobalAPIRateLimit()` is the only limiter in the chain, an attacker can hammer this endpoint far harder than the login endpoint the same file protects with `CriticalRateLimit()` - including racing it during the window between process start and an operator completing setup, when any internal initialised-check is by definition not yet satisfied. Successful abuse of a setup endpoint on a service that holds upstream provider keys, user token keys and billing state is full instance compromise.
findings.evidence: Lines 21-22 register GET and POST /api/setup with no middleware beyond the apiRouter chain, while lines 68-69 give both `middleware.CriticalRateLimit()` and `middleware.TurnstileCheck()` to /user/register and /user/login.

findings.title: Upstream provider content-safety filters are disabled by default (GEMINI_SAFETY_SETTING=BLOCK_NONE, COHERE_SAFETY_SETTING=NONE)
findings.impact: Every tenant of a multi-user gateway inherits an unfiltered upstream by default. The operator carries the resulting content-policy and abuse exposure without having made a decision, and cannot tell from the running system that a decision was made for them.
findings.evidence: Line 110 `GeminiSafetySetting = GetEnvOrDefaultString("GEMINI_SAFETY_SETTING", "BLOCK_NONE")` and line 111 `CohereSafetySetting = GetEnvOrDefaultString("COHERE_SAFETY_SETTING", "NONE")` - both default literals are the providers' OFF sentinels.

findings.title: Log directory created world-writable with mode 0777 and an existence probe that fails open
findings.impact: A local principal on the host (threat-model actor A4) can create, rename, delete or symlink entries inside a directory owned by the gateway process: truncate or doctor the billing/abuse evidence the gateway writes there, read whatever prompt and error material lands in the log files, or pre-plant a file or symlink at a name the logger will later open. No sticky bit is set on the directory, so removing and replacing files created by the gateway is permitted to any local user. The swallowed os.Stat error additionally means a mis-permissioned log path is not reported at boot, and the Mkdir/MkdirAll choice turns an ordinary nested log path into a hard boot failure (availability, gateway availability being a CRITICAL asset in the threat model).
findings.evidence: Line 74 `err = os.Mkdir(*LogDir, 0777)`; the preceding probe at line 73 tests only `os.IsNotExist(err)`, so any other Stat failure silently skips creation.
findings.sanity_triage_applied: Local Attack Vector; Internal/Nested; Static Confirmation

findings.title: Dify debug mode defaults to enabled, contradicting the file's own opt-in convention for debug flags
findings.impact: Every deployment that does not explicitly set DIFY_DEBUG=false runs the Dify relay path in debug mode. The exposure class for a debug flag on a relay path is verbose logging of request/response material, i.e. customer prompts and upstream errors written to the log directory -- the same directory this file creates with mode 0777 at line 74, which makes the two defaults compound: verbose relay logging into a world-writable directory. Because the flag is read from a global set once at boot, disabling it requires a restart.
findings.evidence: Line 134 `constant.DifyDebug = GetEnvOrDefaultBool("DIFY_DEBUG", true)`, against line 82 `DebugEnabled = os.Getenv("DEBUG") == "true"`, line 149 `GENERATE_DEFAULT_TOKEN, false` and line 151 `ERROR_LOG_ENABLED, false`.

findings.title: TLS_INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFY disables certificate validation process-wide by mutating http.DefaultTransport, far beyond the upstream relay
findings.impact: An operator enabling one insecure upstream unknowingly disables certificate validation for the identity providers that authenticate every user of the gateway. An attacker positioned on the network path -- a hostile egress proxy, a compromised DNS resolver, a shared cloud network -- can then impersonate the OIDC/GitHub/Discord endpoint, forge the token exchange and log in as any user, including root, without touching a certificate authority. The same position allows tampering with fetched OIDC discovery documents and pricing/ratio data. Because the in-place mutation is never reversed and never logged, the weakened posture is invisible in operation.
findings.evidence: Lines 88-93 mutate `http.DefaultTransport` - the process-wide default transport - setting `tr.TLSClientConfig.InsecureSkipVerify = true`, rather than configuring a relay-scoped client.
findings.sanity_triage_applied: Documented Insecure Configuration; Non-Default Configuration; Internal/Nested; Static Confirmation

findings.title: Node role defaults to master: any NODE_TYPE value other than the exact lowercase string "slave" makes the replica a master node
findings.impact: In a horizontally scaled deployment, one misspelled or case-wrong environment value silently promotes a replica to master, so master-only scheduled work runs on several nodes at once. For a gateway whose master duties include quota and billing batch updates, that is duplicated or racing writes to financial state rather than a mere availability wobble.
findings.evidence: Line 84 `IsMasterNode = os.Getenv("NODE_TYPE") != "slave"` - every value except the exact lowercase "slave" yields master, while line 82 uses the fail-closed `== "true"` idiom for the adjacent flag.

findings.title: Account-binding OAuth endpoints are registered without UserAuth while every other account-mutating route carries it
findings.impact: If any of the three handlers does not itself re-establish the caller identity, an unauthenticated request can attach an attacker-controlled external identity to an account, which is an account-takeover primitive. Rated LOW because the claim cannot be closed without the absent handler bodies.
findings.evidence: Lines 46, 49 and 51 bind EmailBind / WeChatBind / TelegramBind with only `middleware.CriticalRateLimit()`, while the matching read and unbind routes for the same objects are inside the `UserAuth()` group at lines 122-123.

findings.title: Payment callbacks accept unauthenticated GET and carry no rate limiting, with the webhook environment selector left entirely to an absent handler
findings.impact: An unthrottled, unauthenticated endpoint that credits account balances is an ideal target for offline-to-online signature brute forcing, replay of a single captured callback, and race-condition double-crediting -- none of which the router slows down in any way. Query-string delivery leaks the callback secret material into every log tier that touches the request. If the absent WaffoPancakeWebhook honours a test environment on the production deployment (or fails open on an unrecognised :env), an attacker signs a callback with the sandbox credentials, which vendors publish or share freely, and mints real gateway credit.
findings.evidence: Lines 56-58, 61, 75 and 179 register the payment callbacks with no middleware at all, while line 97 gives the authenticated `/topup` a `CriticalRateLimit()`. Lines 76, 180 and 181 additionally bind the same callbacks to GET.

findings.title: State-changing operations exposed over GET, including access-token generation, making them CSRF- and prefetch-triggerable
findings.impact: A logged-in user who loads any attacker-controlled page -- or whose browser prefetches a link, or whose chat client unfurls a URL -- silently issues GET /api/user/token. If that regenerates the access token, every integration the victim has configured breaks and the old token is invalidated: a one-image, zero-click denial of service against any user, repeatable at will since the route carries no CriticalRateLimit. GET /api/user/logout is the same trick for forced session termination. On the admin side, a single unfurled link in an admin's browser fans out UpdateAllChannelsBalance or TestAllChannels across every upstream provider, burning real upstream quota and money and producing an outbound request storm attributable to the operator's own infrastructure.
findings.evidence: Line 87 `selfRoute.GET("/token", controller.GenerateAccessToken)` binds a GET to a handler named Generate; lines 236, 238 and 239 bind GET to TestAllChannels, UpdateAllChannelsBalance and UpdateChannelBalance. No CSRF middleware appears anywhere in the file.
